Summary

Baruch Goldstein was born Benjamin Carl Goldstein in Brooklyn, New York in 1956 to an Orthodox Jewish family. In the 1970s, he became a charter member of the Jewish Defense League (JDL), a militant organization founded by Rabbi Meir Kahane. After graduating from Yeshiva University's Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Goldstein emigrated to Israel in 1983. He served as a physician in the Israel Defense Forces and later settled in Kiryat Arba, an extremist settlement adjacent to Hebron. Goldstein was an active member of Kach, Kahane's ultranationalist party, and was third on its list for the 1984 Knesset elections. Israeli press reported that Goldstein refused to treat Arabs, even Arab soldiers serving in the IDF, believing it violated Jewish religious law to treat non-Jews. He compared Israel's democracy to Nazism and wore a yellow star marked 'JUDE' in protest. In the weeks before the massacre, Goldstein made ominous statements and was involved in violent incidents at the mosque, including pouring acid on carpets. Palestinian authorities wrote to Prime Minister Rabin warning about Goldstein's dangerous behavior, but no action was taken.

On the morning of February 25, 1994, the 15th day of Ramadan, worshippers noticed the unusual absence of Israeli soldiers from their normal positions around the Ibrahimi Mosque despite tensions the previous evening. At approximately 5:30 AM, as Imam Khalil Muhsen Jabari led hundreds in Fajr (dawn) prayer, Goldstein entered the Isaac Hall—the main prayer area—dressed in his IDF reserve uniform and carrying a Galil assault rifle and pistol. He positioned himself behind a pillar at the rear of the hall. When worshippers prostrated (sujood position), Goldstein opened fire. He reloaded multiple times, methodically shooting prostrate worshippers who were trapped and defenseless. Survivors report the shooting continued for ten minutes. Some eyewitnesses claim they saw additional gunmen, though Israeli investigations denied this. When worshippers finally overcame Goldstein, they beat him to death. By then, 29 Palestinians lay dead—including children as young as 11—and 125 were wounded.

The horror did not end with the shooting. Israeli soldiers present at the mosque closed the gates, trapping survivors inside with the dead and wounded, and preventing medical help from entering. When the gates finally opened, Israeli forces fired on protesters outside, killing more Palestinians. Over the next three weeks, as news of the massacre spread, Palestinians rioted throughout Hebron and the West Bank. Israeli forces killed at least 25 more Palestinians during these protests, including at victims' funerals. The total death toll reached 50-60. Israel's response was to punish the victims: a six-month closure of Hebron; formation of the one-sided Shamgar Commission whose recommendations all favored settlers; partition of the Ibrahimi Mosque giving 60% to Jews (who comprised 0.003% of Hebron's population); closure of 520 businesses and 1,800 shops in the Old City; sealing of Shuhada Street (the main commercial artery); and a network of military checkpoints suffocating Palestinian life. The massacre achieved Goldstein's goal: it did not stop Oslo, but it transformed Hebron into a strangled city, its Old City a ghost town, its Palestinian population subjected to daily humiliation while a few hundred extremist settlers lived under heavy military protection.

War crimes

Mass Murder / Terrorist Attack
Baruch Goldstein massacred 29 unarmed Palestinian worshippers during prayer in deliberate terrorist attack. Premeditated mass murder of civilians in place of worship. Goldstein member of Kach, designated terrorist organization. Attack aimed to derail Oslo peace process by provoking Palestinian retaliation.
Institute for Palestine Studies
Israeli Military Facilitation and Complicity
Suspicious absence of Israeli soldiers from usual positions despite previous evening's tensions. Soldiers present during massacre closed gates, trapping survivors with dead and wounded, preventing medical aid. Many Palestinians believe Israeli military had foreknowledge and facilitated attack. Shamgar Commission whitewashed these issues.
Eyewitness Documentation
Collective Punishment of Victims
Rather than protect Palestinians or remove settlers after massacre, Israel: closed Hebron for 6 months; partitioned Ibrahimi Mosque favoring settlers (60% to Jews); closed 520 businesses and 1,800 shops; sealed Shuhada Street; erected checkpoint network. Violated Geneva Convention Article 33: collective punishment prohibited.
Middle East Monitor
Killing of Palestinian Protesters
Israeli forces killed at least 25 Palestinians during protests following massacre—shot while expressing grief and anger over attack. Use of lethal force against protesters grossly excessive and disproportionate. Many killed at victims' funerals.
WAFA Documentation
Failure to Protect Civilians
Israeli authorities ignored warnings about Goldstein's dangerous behavior months before massacre. Goldstein had attacked mosque previously (acid on carpets), yet no preventive action taken. After massacre, Israel failed to implement UN Security Council Resolution 904 calling for protection of Palestinian civilians and disarming of settlers.
Documentation
Religious Site Appropriation
Following massacre of Muslim worshippers, Israel partitioned Ibrahimi Mosque—giving 60% to Jewish worship despite Jews being 0.003% of Hebron population. Appropriation of sacred Islamic site as collective punishment. During certain Jewish holidays, entire mosque closed to Muslims—at site of their victimization.
Hebron Rehabilitation Committee
Economic Strangulation of Palestinian Community
Closure of 520 businesses and 1,800 shops destroyed Hebron Old City economy. Sealing of Shuhada Street—once thriving commercial center—created ghost town. Mass unemployment, displacement. Economic warfare as collective punishment for being victims of massacre.

Legal classification

Fourth Geneva Convention - Violations
Article 27: 'Protected persons...shall at all times be humanely treated, and shall be protected especially against all acts of violence or threats thereof.' Israel failed to protect Palestinians from settler violence; facilitated attack through military absence.
International Human Rights Law
Right to Life (ICCPR Article 6): Israel failed duty to protect life by ignoring warnings about Goldstein; soldiers' actions during and after massacre facilitated deaths; excessive force against protesters violated right to life.
UN Security Council Resolution 904 (1994)
Condemnation: Security Council 'strongly condemns the massacre...and calls it abhorrent.'
Terrorism and International Criminal Law
Act of Terrorism: Massacre meets all definitions of terrorism—premeditated attack on civilians to achieve political goal (derailing peace process).
Fourth Geneva Convention - Violations
Article 33: 'No protected person may be punished for an offence he or she has not personally committed. Collective penalties...are prohibited.' Six-month closure, business closures, mosque partition, Shuhada Street sealing all constituted collective punishment.
International Human Rights Law
Freedom of Religion (ICCPR Article 18): Partition of Ibrahimi Mosque and restrictions on Muslim worship violated right to freedom of religion and worship.
UN Security Council Resolution 904 (1994)
Protection Measures: Called for 'measures to be taken to guarantee the safety and protection of Palestinian civilians throughout the occupied territory, including, inter alia, a temporary international or foreign presence.' Israel never implemented.
Terrorism and International Criminal Law
Crimes Against Humanity: Part of widespread attack on Palestinian civilian population; systematic persecution.
Fourth Geneva Convention - Violations
Article 53: 'Any destruction...of property...is prohibited, except where such destruction is rendered absolutely necessary by military operations.' Economic strangulation of Old City had no military necessity.
International Human Rights Law
Right to Non-Discrimination: Grossly unequal treatment—Palestinians collectively punished while settler population protected and expanded.
UN Security Council Resolution 904 (1994)
Disarmament: Implicitly called for disarming of settlers. Israel ignored; settlers armed and expanded.
Terrorism and International Criminal Law
State Responsibility: Israel's failure to prevent attack despite warnings, facilitation through military absence, collective punishment of victims, and failure to implement UNSC Resolution 904 constitute state responsibility for violations.
UN Security Council Resolution 904 (1994)
Implementation: Israel never complied with any provision of Resolution 904.

Commanders

1956-1994 (killed by survivors) Baruch Goldstein (born Benjamin Carl Goldstein)
US-born Israeli settler, physician, IDF reserve officer, Kach member. Massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers during Ramadan prayer. Acted to derail Oslo peace process. Revered as martyr by far-right extremists; grave in Kiryat Arba became pilgrimage site.
1932-1990 (assassinated in New York) Meir Kahane
US-born extremist rabbi. Founded Jewish Defense League (JDL) and Kach party. Advocated expulsion of all Arabs from Israel/Palestine, Jewish supremacy. Goldstein was follower. Kahane assassinated 1990, but ideology lives on through followers and current Israeli far-right parties.
1922-1995 (assassinated) Yitzhak Rabin
Condemned Goldstein's act rhetorically but government implemented collective punishment against Palestinian victims. Led Oslo peace process Goldstein sought to derail. Assassinated by Israeli extremist in 1995.
1925-2019 Meir Shamgar
Former Israeli Supreme Court President who led commission investigating massacre. Report concluded Goldstein acted alone (denying military complicity), recommended measures that all burdened Palestinians. Criticized as whitewash.
1976-present Itamar Ben-Gvir
Former Kach activist who hung portrait of Goldstein in his home. Now serves in Israeli government as National Security Minister. Represents continuation of Goldstein's ideology in Israeli mainstream politics. Visited Goldstein's grave and praised him.
